source_text: 31.11 διὰ δὲ τὴν ἄρρητον αὐτοῦ ἐνανθρώπησιν ἐπήγαγεν τό «ὁ θεός σου». 31.12 Καὶ ἐν ρμδʹ. «ἡ βασιλεία σου βασιλεία πάντων τῶν αἰώνων καὶ ἡ δεσποτεία σου ἐν πάσῃ γενεᾷ καὶ γενεᾷ». 31.13 καὶ ἐν τῷ ιʹ ψαλμῷ· «βασιλεύσει κύριος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος». 31.14 Καὶ Πέτρῳ δὲ ὁ υἱὸς τὰς κλεῖς ὡς κύριος δέδωκεν τῆς βασιλείας–οὐ τοῦ νῦν αἰῶνος, οὔπω γὰρ τυγχάνομεν αὐτῆς, ἀλλὰ τοῦ μέλλοντος, ἐν ᾧ καὶ παραδιδόναι αὐτὸν τεκμαίρονται αἱρετικοί–ἐπὶ τὸ εἰσδεχθῆναι μὲν τοὺς ἄναρχον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπέραντον τὴν βασιλείαν εἶναι πιστεύοντας, ἀπωσθῆναι δέ, ὡς μικρῷ 36 πρόσθεν εἴρηται, τοὺς μὴ κράζοντας κατὰ τὸν Ναθαναήλ· «σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Χριστιανῶν». 31.15 Καὶ τὴν προφητείαν δὲ Ἠσαΐου τὴν λέγουσαν· «τὸν βασιλέα κύριον Σαβαὼθ εἶδον τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς μου». Παῦλος μὲν τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἀνέθηκεν, Ἰωάννης δὲ τῷ μονογενεῖ, ὡς προείρηται, διὰ τὸ ἐπίκοινον τῆς θεότητος καὶ τῆς ἀδιαδόχου μιᾶς βασιλείας. 31.16 πῶς γὰρ καὶ ἐγχωρεῖ, τὸν μὲν ἄρχειν, τὸν δὲ ὡς ἐν ἀνθρώποις σχολαῖον εἶναι, ὅταν ὁ πατὴρ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ καὶ ὁ υἱὸς ἐν τῷ πατρὶ μένει καὶ ὁπότε τὸ πνεῦμα ἐκπορεύεται παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ μένει παρὰ τῷ υἱῷ θεϊκῶς; 32.ν Περὶ δοξολογίας αὐτοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ. 32.1 Τοιγαροῦν καὶ περὶ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ θέα, οἷα καὶ αὖθις μαρτυροῦσιν οἱ ἅγιοι, «ὧν», φησίν, «ὁ κόσμος οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος», διδάσκοντες ἡμᾶς τοὺς χάριτι ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κληθέντας υἱούς, τὸν ἐκ τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ πατρὸς μονογενῆ υἱὸν ἐν ἴσῃ καθάπερ αὐτὸν δοξάζειν δόξῃ καὶ ἀποβλέπειν εἰς τὴν δόξαν, ἣν εἶχεν πρὸ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ τῷ μὴ φθονοῦντι τῷ ἀγαπητῷ. 32.2 βασκανίας γὰρ καὶ παντὸς πάθους τὸ θεῖον ἐλεύθερον. 32.3 ∆αυῒδ ἐν οαʹ ψαλμῷ, ὃν ὁμολογουμένως περὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ προεφήτευσεν, «ἔσται», φησίν, «τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ εὐλογημένον εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· πρὸ τοῦ ἡλίου διαμενεῖ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ πρὸ τῆς σελήνης γενεὰς γενεῶν. καὶ ἐνευλογηθή σονται ἐν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη μακαριοῦσιν αὐτόν. εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια μόνος, καὶ εὐλογητὸν τὸ ὄνομα τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος. καὶ πλη ρωθήσεται τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ. γένοιτο». 32.4 «εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς Ἰσραήλ» εἶπεν ἀντὶ τοῦ· «δοξαζόμενος» ἢ «αἰνούμενος». 32.5 ὁ γὰρ θεὸς εὐλογεῖται μὲν ὑπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ, τουτέστιν δοξάζεται· εὐλογεῖ δὲ αὐτὸς τὰ οἰκεῖα κτίσματα, τουτέστιν ἁγιάζει. 32.6 ἐπισημαντέον δέ, ὡς καὶ θεὸς Ἰσραήλ, ὅ ἐστι θεὸς τῶν πατέρων, καθὰ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἀνείρηται. 32.7 Καὶ ἐν πεʹ ψαλμῷ τὸ παγκρατορικὸν καὶ πανδύναμον τοῦ μονογενοῦς καὶ ὡς ὀφείλεται δοξάζεσθαι παριστῶν ψάλλει· «πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, ὅσα ἐποίησας, ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιόν σου, κύριε, καὶ δοξάσουσιν τὸ ὄνομά σου, ὅτι μέγας εἶ σὺ καὶ ποιῶν θαυμάσια· σὺ εἶ ὁ θεὸς μόνος». 32.8 Καὶ ἐν ιηʹ· «οἱ οὐρανοὶ διηγοῦνται δόξαν θεοῦ». 32.9 πῶς; τῷ δεικνύναι ἀπὸ τῆς δοθείσης αὐτοῖς μεγαλειότητος καὶ ὡραιότητος ἀνυπέρβλητον καὶ δοξαζόμενον τὸν δημιουργήσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς λόγος. 32.10 «τῷ» γάρ «λόγῳ κυρίου οἱ οὐρανοὶ ἐστερεώθησαν καὶ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ αἱ δυνάμεις αὐτῶν». 32.11 οὔτε οὖν τὴν τῶν ἀψύχων αἰσχύνονται περὶ τῆς δόξης τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος μαρτυρίαν. 32.12 Καὶ ἐν κγʹ· «ἄρατε πύλας, οἱ ἄρχοντες, ὑμῶν καὶ ἐπάρθητε, πύλαι αἰώνιοι, καὶ εἰσελεύ σεται ὁ βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης». 32.13 παρακελεύεται τῇ μὲν κάτω κτίσει ἆραι τὰς πύλας ἐν τῇ ἐνανθρωπήσει αὐτοῦ, τῇ δὲ ἄνω ἐν τῇ ἀναλήψει. 32.14 Καὶ ἐν ριϛʹ· «αἰνεῖτε τὸν κύριον, πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐπαινεσάτωσαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ λαοί». 32.15 Ἠσαΐας δέ· «βασιλέα μετὰ δόξης ὄψεσθε». 32.16 Ἐζεκιὴλ δέ· «εὐλογημένη ἡ δόξα κυρίου ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτοῦ» καί «αὕτη ἡ ὅρασις ὁμοίωμα δόξης κυρίου». 32.17 Εἶτα Παῦλος· «φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρ του θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου». 32.18 καὶ πάλιν Ῥωμαίοις· 32.18 «διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρ σίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς. οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογημένος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν». 32.19 τίς δὲ ὁ πάντων δημιουργός, ὃν εἶναι λέγει εὐλογητὸν εἰς 37
pass_a_gloss: 31.11 And because of his unspeakable becoming-man he added 'your God'. 31.12 And in [Psalm] 144 (Greek numbering; Psalm 145 in English): 'your kingdom is a kingdom of all the ages, and your lordship in every generation and generation'. 31.13 And in the 10th psalm: 'the Lord will reign into the age of the age'. 31.14 And to Peter the Son gave as Lord the keys of the kingdom (not of the present age, for we do not yet obtain it, but of the one to come, in which the heretics also conjecture him to hand [it] over) toward the being received of those who believe his kingdom to be beginningless and boundless, and the being thrust away, as was said a little [page number 36] before, of those not crying out according to Nathanael: 'you are the Son of God, you are the King of the Christians'. 31.15 And the prophecy of Isaiah which says: 'I saw the King, Lord Sabaoth, with my eyes', Paul referred to the Spirit of God, and John to the only-begotten, as was said before, because of the commonness of the Godhead and of the one kingdom without succession. 31.16 For how is it even admissible that the one rules and the other is at leisure, as among men, when the Father abides in the Son and the Son in the Father and when the Spirit proceeds from the Father and abides beside the Son divinely? 32.ν [Chapter title:] About the glorifying of the Son of God himself. 32.1 Therefore, about his glory too, look at the sort of things the saints testify again, those 'of whom', it says, 'the world was not worthy', teaching us, who by grace on the earth were called sons, to glorify the only-begotten Son from the hypostasis of the Father with glory equal just as him, and to look toward the glory which he had before the world was, beside the Father who does not begrudge the beloved. 32.2 For the divine is free of envy and of every passion. 32.3 David in the 71st psalm (Greek numbering; Psalm 72 in English), which admittedly he prophesied about the Christ, says: 'his name will be blessed into the ages; before the sun his name will remain, and before the moon generations of generations. And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him, and all the nations will call him blessed. Blessed [be] the Lord, the God of Israel, the one doing wonders alone, and blessed the name of his glory into the age and into the age of the age. And all the earth will be filled with his glory. May it be'. 32.4 'Blessed [be] the Lord the God of Israel' he said in place of 'being glorified' or 'being praised'. 32.5 For God is blessed by his works, that is, glorified; but he himself blesses his own creatures, that is, sanctifies [them]. 32.6 And it must be noted that [he is] also God of Israel, which is God of the fathers, as his Father has been proclaimed. 32.7 And in the 85th psalm (Greek numbering; Psalm 86 in English), presenting the all-ruling and all-powerful [nature] of the only-begotten and that he is owed to be glorified, he sings: 'all the nations, as many as you made, will come and worship before you, Lord, and will glorify your name, because you are great and doing wonders; you are God alone'. 32.8 And in the 18th (Psalm 19 in English): 'the heavens tell the glory of God'. 32.9 How? By showing from the greatness and beauty given to them the one who crafted [them], who is God the Word, unsurpassable and glorified. 32.10 For 'by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm and by the spirit of his mouth their powers'. 32.11 So they are not even ashamed before the testimony of the soulless things about the glory of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. 32.12 And in the 23rd (Psalm 24 in English): 'lift your gates, you rulers, and be lifted up, everlasting gates, and the King of the glory will enter'. 32.13 He urges the creation below to lift the gates at his becoming-man, and the one above at the taking-up. 32.14 And in the 116th (Psalm 117 in English): 'praise the Lord, all the nations, and let all the peoples praise him'. 32.15 And Isaiah: 'you will see a king with glory'. 32.16 And Ezekiel: 'blessed the glory of the Lord from his place' and 'this vision [is] a likeness of glory of the Lord'. 32.17 Then Paul: 'claiming to be wise they were made foolish and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God in a likeness of an image of corruptible man'. 32.18 And again to the Romans: [the repeated number 32.18 is debris] 'therefore he handed them over in the desires of their hearts into uncleanness, of their bodies being dishonoured among themselves; who exchanged the glory of God in the lie, and revered and served the creation beside the one who created, who is blessed into the ages; amen'. 32.19 And who is the craftsman of all, whom he says to be blessed into [page number 37; the sentence continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: Because of his ineffable incarnation he added “your God” (Psalm 45:7). And in the hundred and forty-fifth Psalm: “Your kingdom is a kingdom of all the ages, and your dominion is in every generation and generation” (Psalm 145:13). And in the tenth Psalm: “The Lord will reign for ever and ever” (Psalm 10:16).

And to Peter the Son, as Lord, gave the keys of the kingdom: not of the present age, for we do not yet possess it, but of the age to come, the one in which the heretics guess that he even hands it over. He gave them so that those who believe his kingdom to be without beginning and without end should be admitted, and, as was said a little earlier, those should be thrust away who do not cry out with Nathanael: “You are the Son of God, you are the King of the Christians” (John 1:49).

And the prophecy of Isaiah that says, “I have seen with my eyes the King, the Lord of hosts” (Isaiah 6:5), Paul referred to the Spirit of God (Acts 28:25), and John, as was said before, to the Only-begotten (John 12:41), because the Godhead is shared and the one kingdom has no successor. For how could it even be that one rules and the other sits idle, as happens among men, when the Father abides in the Son and the Son in the Father (John 14:10), and when the Spirit proceeds from the Father (John 15:26) and abides with the Son in a divine way?
On the glorifying of the Son of God himself.

So look, then, at what the saints testify once more about his glory, those “of whom,” it says, “the world was not worthy” (Hebrews 11:38). They teach us, who on earth have been called sons by grace, to glorify the only-begotten Son, who is from the substance of the Father, with a glory equal to his, and to look to the glory that he had with the Father before the world existed (John 17:5); for the Father does not begrudge the Beloved. The divine is free from envy and from every passion.

David, in the seventy-second Psalm, which by common consent he prophesied about Christ, says: “His name shall be blessed for ever; his name shall endure before the sun, and before the moon for generations of generations. And all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed in him; all the nations shall call him blessed. Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders; and blessed be the name of his glory for ever and for ever and ever. And the whole earth shall be filled with his glory. So be it” (Psalm 72:17-19).

He said “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel” in place of “glorified” or “praised.” For God is blessed by his works, that is, glorified; and he himself blesses his own creatures, that is, sanctifies them. And it should be noted that he is also God of Israel, that is, God of the fathers, just as his Father has been proclaimed.

And in the eighty-sixth Psalm, setting forth the almighty and all-powerful nature of the Only-begotten and that he ought to be glorified, he sings: “All the nations you have made shall come and worship before you, Lord, and shall glorify your name; for you are great and do wonders; you alone are God” (Psalm 86:9-10).

And in the nineteenth: “The heavens declare the glory of God” (Psalm 19:1). How? By showing, from the greatness and beauty given them, that the one who made them, God the Word, is unsurpassable and glorified. For “by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the Spirit of his mouth all their powers” (Psalm 33:6). So they are not even put to shame by the witness of lifeless things to the glory of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

And in the twenty-fourth: “Lift up your gates, you rulers, and be lifted up, you everlasting gates, and the King of glory shall come in” (Psalm 24:7). He bids the creation below lift up the gates at his incarnation, and the creation above at his ascension. And in the hundred and seventeenth: “Praise the Lord, all you nations, and let all the peoples praise him” (Psalm 117:1).

And Isaiah: “You shall see a king with glory” (Isaiah 33:17). And Ezekiel: “Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place” (Ezekiel 3:12), and, “This vision is the likeness of the glory of the Lord” (Ezekiel 1:28).

Then Paul: “Claiming to be wise, they became fools, and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man” (Romans 1:22-23). And again to the Romans: “Therefore he gave them up in the desires of their hearts to impurity, to the dishonouring of their bodies among themselves. They exchanged the glory of God for a lie, and worshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen” (Romans 1:24-25). And who is the maker of all, whom he says is blessed for …

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, wrong psalm numbers, printed edition numbers
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed (31.11)-(32.3) after its sentences, kept Greek numbers (Psalm 144, Psalm 105) and invented others (Psalm 92 for the tenth Psalm, 'fifteenth' for the hundred and sixteenth), made the heretics say the Son 'is to be handed over' and his kingdom 'without ruler' (31.14), had Paul 'dedicate' the prophecy and the Son be 'a mere pastime' (31.15-31.16), made the Beloved the one 'who does not envy' (it is the Father), rendered βασκανία as 'flattery', οἰκεῖα κτίσματα as 'resident creatures', and ἀνείρηται as 'was carried up' (32.6), split Psalm 72:17-19 across two paragraphs, garbled 32.9, and used 'thy', 'unto', 'Wherefore' and the filler [Psalm]. References: Greek Psalms 144, 10, 71, 85, 18, 23, 116 rendered as the hundred and forty-fifth, tenth, seventy-second, eighty-sixth, nineteenth, twenty-fourth and hundred and seventeenth (Psalms 145:13, 10:16, 72:17-19, 86:9-10, 19:1, 24:7, 117:1); Romans 1:23 widened to 1:22-23; Psalm 45:7, Acts 28:25, John 12:41, John 14:10, John 15:26 and John 17:5 added; abbreviations written in full.

choices.why: The verse is LXX Psalm 9:37, which in Hebrew and English numbering is Psalm 10:16; Didymus' 'tenth' agrees with the English number, so it stands.

choices.term: ἐν ᾧ καὶ παραδιδόναι αὐτὸν τεκμαίρονται αἱρετικοί
choices.english: the one in which the heretics guess that he even hands it over
choices.why: αὐτόν is the subject of the infinitive (the Son hands over the kingdom), not its object; the old 'he is to be handed over' reversed it.
Didymus' wording; John 1:49 has 'King of Israel'. Kept as he quotes it and noted in problems.
ἀνατίθημι here means to ascribe a text to someone; Paul ascribes the Isaiah 6 vision to the Holy Spirit (Acts 28:25), John to the Son (John 12:41).
σχολαῖος is a person at leisure, out of office: one ruler reigns while the other has retired. 'Mere pastime' (old draft) mistook it for σχολή as amusement.
Read as the imperative 'look' (θεάομαι), which the dependent οἷα clause requires.

choices.term: τῷ πατρὶ τῷ μὴ φθονοῦντι τῷ ἀγαπητῷ
choices.english: for the Father does not begrudge the Beloved
choices.why: The participle agrees with τῷ πατρί; the Beloved (the Son) is its object. The old draft made the Beloved the one who does not envy.

choices.english: with a glory equal to his
choices.why: αὐτόν is the Father, glorified in the same way; English folds the comparison into 'equal to his'.

choices.english: by the Spirit of his mouth
choices.why: Didymus reads Psalm 33:6 of the Holy Spirit, as his next sentence shows ('the glory of the Son and of the Holy Spirit'), so 'Spirit' is capitalized rather than 'breath'.

choices.term: ἐπισημαντέον δέ, ὡς καὶ θεὸς Ἰσραήλ
choices.english: it should be noted that he is also God of Israel
choices.why: Elliptical; the subject is the Christ of the psalm, as the next words ('as his Father has been proclaimed') show. English needs 'he is'; no bracket because no new claim is added.

choices.term: μετήλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει
choices.english: They exchanged the glory of God for a lie
choices.why: Didymus' text of Romans 1:25 reads 'glory' where the New Testament has 'truth'; kept as he quotes it, since this chapter is on glory.

choices.english: whom he says is blessed for …
choices.why: The section ends after εἰς; the page number '37' follows and the sentence continues in the next section, so it ends with an ellipsis.
Split words (ἐνευλογηθή σονται, πλη ρωθήσεται, εἰσελεύ σεται, ἀφθάρ του, ἀκαθαρ σίαν) read as single words; the page numbers 36 and 37 and the repeated paragraph number 32.18 skipped.
